lines.text: Extra, extra. A language model says something false, and says it with confidence.
Why? A language model is trained to pick a likely next word.
Likely is not the same as true.
Ask for a book that does not exist, and it can write a believable title, author and year. They sound right, so they get picked.
One fix is to let the model look things up, and show its sources.
Another is to check every claim against the source yourself. Fluent text is not evidence.
